the current quark masses in the standard model are not small.

the gluon condensates are not only a source of the dynamical mass generation but also a source of enhancement of the current mass.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current quark masses are not as light as we think they should be, but they are still small enough to be consistent with the low-energy phenomenology.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the current quark masses are not the true quark masses of the low-energy QCD effective lagrangian, and that the true quark mass in this lagrangian is larger by a factor ≳4.

the gluon condensates, which are known to be large in QCD, are not negligible in the quark propagators, and that their effects are important to include in phenomenological applications of the quark propagor.

, in the context of a gauge invariant framework, gluon condensates may be used to generate a non-vanishing effective current quark quark mass in the presence of a vanishing true current quark quarks mass.
